About the catalogue

Paint Commons gathers miniature paint information from manufacturers’ publications and community sources into stable, reusable records for painters, contributors, and developers.

Open and reusable

Portable files with stable IDs, free to reuse.

Sources cited

Every colour and barcode names its source and method.

Corrections reviewed

A maintainer reviews each change, and the history is public.

Personal data stays private

Only information someone submits and a maintainer approves is published.

Contribute to the catalogue

Corrections arrive by three routes, and each is reviewed before it joins the public catalogue.

  • GitHub pull requests
  • Correction form on this site
  • Apps that use the catalogue

Add paints or sources

Read the contribution guide ↗
Can I use the data in my own project?

Yes. Download the data or use the catalogue repository on GitHub. The data is CC0 1.0, except records from sources with their own licence; those carry the source’s credit, listed in the repository’s notices.

How accurate are the swatches?

Swatches are approximate. Lighting, camera, surface, and application all change how a paint looks, and metallic and colour-shift paints need more than one value. Each swatch names its source so readers can judge it.

Is any personal information published?

No. Only information someone explicitly submits, and a maintainer approves, becomes part of the catalogue. Correction suggestions are posted publicly on GitHub without the sender’s name or email address.
